narrative.title: The Best-Fit Locker Lookup
narrative.scenario: A sports warehouse shelves gear by size in a sorted tree, and a customer asks for the largest stocked size that still fits their frame — nothing bigger than the measurement. One descent answers it: whenever the current shelf fits, it becomes the running best and the clerk probes for an even better fit on the right; an oversized shelf sends the search left. Running out of tree without any fit means nothing qualifies.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and an integer x — the measurement.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the greatest tree value less than or equal to x, or -1 if every stocked value is bigger.

testCases.explanation: Values at most 6 are 2 and 5 (7 overshoots), so the best fit is 5.
The largest value not exceeding 13 is 10.

hintLevels: Level 1: You want the largest value that doesn't overshoot x — a mirror image of the ceil hunt.
Level 2: Node fits? Log it and try to beat it on the right. Node too big? Its right wing can only be worse — go left.
Level 3: An exact match ends the search; otherwise the last logged value on one descent is the floor.
